solver: cmd/solve, two arms over 8 instances. G0 = -cand-mode mix -cand-global-k 0. G12 = -cand-mode mix -cand-global-k 12. All other flags identical: -rounds 150 -wall-sec 90 -hot-k 6 -peel 6 -model twin -budget-mode full -presolve unmovable -presolve-time 15 -presolve-deep 100 -skip-floor=true -cand-hop-cache=true.
why: The 2026-09-10_03 microbenchmark measured singleton recall at 21.9% and found that on setA-04/10/13/16 the candidate pool does not contain the best singleton that brute-force ranking finds. This experiment measures the fix (a global-relief safety net that routes every node as a singleton) in the outer loop, where it must pay for itself in wall clock as well as in candidate quality.

arms.G0: no net -- the v1 targeted pool, identical to the B arm of 2026-09-10_04
arms.G12: net on, GlobalK=12 -- scan every node as a singleton, append the 12 best-relief ones after the round-robin interleave, with their own emission budget

attribution: The net is additive by construction: it is appended after the interleave (so it cannot shrink any strategy's pool share) and Build step 6 emits it outside MaxW1 (so it cannot displace a pool singleton). Any A/B difference therefore comes from the added nodes alone.

defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: net nodes are the global top-K by relief, so ranking-then-truncating to MaxW1 would push high-relief POOL singletons out of the emitted list -- trading the tail (od_scan's long detours) for the head (the net), since the two are not interchangeable
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: Build step 6 splits the 1-waypoint list by Tag, truncates the pool list to MaxW1, emits the net list outside that budget (it is already bounded by GlobalK), then stable-sorts the union by relief with the pool inserted first so ties favour the pool
defect_found_and_fixed.test: TestGlobalReliefDoesNotDisplacePoolSingletons -- verified to fail pre-fix with 'net displaced pool singleton 3: singles are [9 1 2], want 1,2,3 plus 9'
defect_found_and_fixed.honest_limitation: this defect is NOT why setA-04 lost its tail. setA-04 G12 measured byte-identically before and after the fix (firstbit 581237, tie 1/500, first gap layer 2, 580858 vs 580857, twice). The setA-04 tail loss is a separate, still-unfixed mechanism: 12 extra columns change the MIP's lex-peel trajectory (same firstbit, tie layers 10 -> 1).

decision.cand_global_k_default: kept at 0 (opt-in). The net wins on the small instances at a 90s wall but starves the big ones, and the competition budget is 10 min/instance where that may not bind -- but that has not been measured.
decision.next: bound the net's cost (e.g. replace the full-node scan with a widened hop ball, which the BFS cache makes nearly free) or scale GlobalK with n; then re-measure setA-16/19 at 600s.
